item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it adds only the requested convenience API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, and avoids unrelated retry and API changes. It still needs revision before merge because Upload duplicates Add instead of routing through it and its tests omit several required behaviors.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature and uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required buffered, replayable multipart body.","B preserves the existing FilesOption API and avoids the explicitly forbidden association fields and unrelated retry/request-body refactoring introduced by A.","A adds numerous public association options, NewFileWithFields machinery, Raw.Do retry behavior, body-closing semantics, documentation, and broad tests despite the contract explicitly forbidding association additions and unrelated retry refactors.","Both implementations call Raw.Do directly and duplicate Add's request/response logic, violating the requirement to route the encoded body through FilesService.Add; B's smaller implementation is much easier to correct to `return s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...)`."] ,"risks_a":["Directly violates scope requirements by adding association fields and changing generic request/retry machinery.","Upload uses NewFileWithFields and bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior.","The new adoptRequestBody changes behavior globally for Raw.Do, Files.Add, Update, pictures, and other callers, creating compatibility and ownership risks outside the task contract."] ,"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its logic, so future Add behavior or error-semantic changes may diverge.","The Upload test checks field and filename but never reads and verifies the uploaded content.","Tests do not cover Upload retry with streamed source content, empty-filename/nil-content validation, or propagation of source-reader failures; the generic bytes.Reader retry test is insufficient."]}
